_README: THE EQUIVALENCE CLASSIFICATION — MUTATION-EQUIVALENCE-2026-08-04 §5/§6.1.
A surviving mutant is not automatically a test gap. Some cannot be killed by ANY input: `if (lo < 0)
lo = 0` mutated to `<=` still assigns 0 when lo IS 0. Reporting those against a `killed / tested`
denominator makes the target unreachable by arithmetic and buries the real gaps among them.
Until now this classification lived in BRIEF PROSE, which means every sweep re-litigated the same
survivors and no tool could report it. This file is that prose made machine-readable, and it is
consumed by `tools/mutate.mjs` (see `classifySurvivors`) so a run reports `killed / distinguishable`
beside the raw rate rather than instead of it.
MATCHED ON (line, op, before) — the same key `findCanary` uses. `after` is recorded for a reader,
not for matching, so a change to the mutation operator's output text does not silently orphan an
entry.
THE CLASSES, and they are not interchangeable:
· no-distinguishing-input  — a battery of inputs was run against original and mutant and every
one produced byte-identical output. STRONG EVIDENCE, NOT PROOF: a
proof needs an argument over the whole input domain. `probe` records
what was actually run, so the claim can be re-checked or widened.
· untestable-by-design     — a log string, or a branch unreachable by construction. The argument
goes in `why` and must be about the CODE, not about the test suite.
· real-gap                 — killable, no test yet. These stay in the distinguishable denominator;
they are debt, not equivalence. An entry here is a TODO, not an excuse.
THIS FILE CANNOT FLATTER A RATE, BY CONSTRUCTION. `mutate.mjs` reports three failure modes loudly:
· REFUTED  — an entry claims equivalence and the mutant was KILLED. The classification is WRONG;
a distinguishing input exists after all. Fix the entry, never the test.
· ORPHANED — an entry matches no generated mutant (the line moved, or the code changed). It is
excluded from every count until re-verified, so a stale entry shrinks nothing.
· unclassified survivors are counted and named, so silence is never mistaken for equivalence.
Only `no-distinguishing-input` and `untestable-by-design` leave the denominator. `real-gap` does not.

EDITING THIS FILE: match its existing indent and trailing newline, and check the DIFF SIZE is proportional to the change. A json round-trip at the wrong indent rewrote all 5,653 lines on 2026-10-05 (#3297) — a wholesale reformat of a ledger four sessions append to, in which another session's entry would be invisible, and no gate inspects formatting. clock.js.why: KILLABLE and now killed — `{window: 0}` is accepted as a window, so `win >> 1` is 0, the running median collapses to a single point and stops smoothing silently. Listed here so the classification is complete, NOT to excuse it: it stays in the distinguishable denominator.

cpap_edf.py.key: - [0] * n_records) # values are recomputed on write; placeholders here | + [1] * n_records) # values are recomputed on write; placeholders here
cpap_edf.py.probe: same lane, same reasoning: the placeholder value is never emitted.
cpap_edf.py.why: A PROOF: the Crc16 lane's samples are placeholders that write_edf NEVER reads — it recomputes the checksum from the other signals' bytes per record (crc16_ccitt), and read-back overwrites them with those computed values. So [0], [1], or None all produce byte-identical output. No input distinguishes.

cpap_edf_writer.py.probe: Built a full 61-batch BRP.edf twice — once with _closed seeded False, once None — then double-closed each: the written bytes are byte-identical between the two seeds, and the second close is a verified no-op (same bytes, same mtime) under both. Run empirically 2026-08-23.
cpap_edf_writer.py.why: A PROOF over the init value: `self._closed` seeds the idempotent-close guard and is read ONLY by `if self._closed:` in close() — both False and None are falsy, so the first close proceeds identically, after which close() sets it True. No other path reads the init value. So False, None (or any falsy seed) produce identical behaviour and identical output. The mutant surfaced here only because the §2 controller-fix added _interval_checked to __init__, pulling the whole function into diff-scope (#1701).

cpap_edf_writer.py.key: - return calendar.timegm((y, mo, d, hh, mm, ss, 0, 0, 0)) * 1000.0 | + return calendar.timegm((y, mo, d, hh, mm, ss, 1, 0, 0)) * 1000.0
cpap_edf_writer.py.probe: Swept tm_wday/tm_yday/tm_isdst over {0,1,6,-1,99} x {0,1,366,-1} x {0,1,-1} across five dates (2026-08-23, 2000-02-29 leap, 1970-01-01 epoch, 2038-01-19, 2026-12-31) — 300 tuples, 0 differed from the (…,0,0,0) reference. Run empirically 2026-08-26.
cpap_edf_writer.py.why: `calendar.timegm` reads ONLY tm_year..tm_sec (the first six struct_time fields); tm_wday, tm_yday and tm_isdst are ignored by construction — unlike `time.mktime`, which consults tm_isdst. So mutating any of the three trailing zeros cannot change the result for any input. This entry covers the tm_wday variant; sibling entries cover tm_yday and tm_isdst.

cpap_edf_writer.py.key: - self._part = None # the .part path once the start is known | + self._part = "" # the .part path once the start is known
cpap_edf_writer.py.probe: every read of `self._part` (close, _flush) is reached only after _set_start has assigned it the .part path; close() returns early while _start is None (read 2026-10-04)
cpap_edf_writer.py.why: the initial value is overwritten before any read: close() returns before touching _part while no start is set, and _flush runs only from on_batch after the start is set.

cpap_record.py.probe: Exercised both variants through the full sink lifecycle — acq_facts before open, on_batch before open, close before open, open, on_batch, acq_facts while open, double-open, double-close, acq_facts after close — comparing every returned value and raised exception type. Identical throughout (300-char normalised dumps). Run empirically 2026-08-26.
cpap_record.py.why: `_fh` is a WRITE-ONLY slot until `open()` assigns the real handle; the only read of its initial value is `acq_facts`'s `self._fh is None` clause, which is already gated behind `self._ever_opened` — False before any open, so the clause is never reached with the initial value in play. Surfaced because adding `_first_device_start` pulled __init__ into diff-scope.

cpap_record.py.probe: Same full-lifecycle sweep as the `_fh` entry above, both variants, comparing every return value and exception type. Identical throughout. Run empirically 2026-08-26.
cpap_record.py.why: Every consumer tests the state against `_OPEN` (`open` refuses if == _OPEN; `on_batch` and `close` return/raise if != _OPEN), and both `_CLOSED` and None are != _OPEN. The one `== _CLOSED` read is in `acq_facts`, gated behind `_ever_opened`, which is False before any open — so the initial value is never observable. Surfaced by the same __init__ re-scoping.

cpap_stream.py.key: - bus.register(key, label, unit, fs, chans=1) | + bus.register(key, label, unit, fs, )
cpap_stream.py.probe: Registered the same stream on two TelemetryBus instances — one with chans=1 explicit, one omitting it — and compared the stored StreamMeta: equal, chans=1 under both. Run empirically 2026-08-23.
cpap_stream.py.why: `TelemetryBus.register(self, key, label, unit, fs, chans=1, labels=())` DEFAULTS chans to 1, so passing chans=1 explicitly and omitting it are the SAME call — the StreamMeta stored is identical. cpap_stream.py.probe: n/a — the argument is about the CODE, not a battery of inputs.

mutation_triage.py.probe: EXHAUSTIVE, run 2026-08-27: every string of length 1-8 over the alphabet {a, b, .} — 9840 strings — compared rsplit('.',1)[-1] vs rsplit('.')[-1] vs rsplit('.',2)[-1]. ZERO counterexamples. Plus the real mutant-name shapes: 'cpap_stream.x_foo__x', 'a.b.c.xǁCǁm', 'x_foo', '.leading', 'trailing.', '..' — all three agree.
mutation_triage.py.why: A PROOF, not a judgement: `rsplit` splits from the RIGHT, so `[-1]` is always the text after the FINAL separator occurrence. Raising maxsplit only adds splits further LEFT, which changes earlier elements and can never change `[-1]`; with no separator present every maxsplit returns `[s]`. So `s.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]`, `s.rsplit('.')[-1]` and `s.rsplit('.', 2)[-1]` are the same value for EVERY string. No input distinguishes them, so no assertion can kill this without asserting on the call's shape rather than its behaviour.

nightqc.py.key: - datetime.fromisoformat(ts), dev_ms=_POLAR_EPOCH_MS + dev_ns / 1e6 | + datetime.fromisoformat(ts), dev_ms=_POLAR_EPOCH_MS + dev_ns / 1000001.0
nightqc.py.probe: Arithmetic, then the real fixture. `dev_ns / 1000001.0` vs `/ 1e6` on a 2026 counter (DEV0_NS = 8.439e17 ns) biases `dev_ms` by a CONSTANT 843,899.2 ms; the part that VARIES across a recording is `elapsed_ms × 1e-6` — measured 28.8 ms over 8 h, 86.4 ms over 24 h, 31,536 ms over a year. Flipping a fall-back fold needs more than 1,800,000 ms, first reached at a span of ~499,320 h (57 years) of continuous recording. Driven through the real seam fixtures (test_nightqc_arrival_quality_resolves_the_repeated_hour_by_the_DEVICE_counter and its two-device sibling) this mutant resolves every fold identically, while the `dev_ms=None`, argument-dropped, sign-flipped and `× 1e6` mutants on the same line are all KILLED by them.
nightqc.py.why: `dev_ms` is consumed for one purpose: choosing between two candidate instants an HOUR apart, by which one keeps `host − dev` closest to the previous row's offset. A constant bias cancels there — it enters `prev_offset_ms` on the previous row and is subtracted on this one — so only the DRIFT of the error matters, and at one part per million of elapsed time that takes decades to reach half an hour. Every other mutation of this argument perturbs it non-uniformly and is killed; this one is a scale error small enough to be absorbed by the estimator it feeds.

nightqc.py.key: - diffs, _tau0_of(pairs), _TDEV_TAU_S, sample_times=[(h - pairs[0][0]) / 1000.0 for h, _, _ in pairs] | + diffs, _tau0_of(pairs), _TDEV_TAU_S, sample_times=[(h - pairs[0][0]) * 1000.0 for h, _, _ in pairs]
nightqc.py.probe: tests/test_pmd_arrival_writer.py::test_probe_the_stability_curve_is_invariant_under_any_POSITIVE_AFFINE_map_of_sample_times — 900 pairs with one real 90 s hole, so the segmentation is non-vacuous (2 segments); the axis is then scaled by 1e6 and by 0.999 and shifted by two different constants. `allan.stability`'s whole record is byte-identical under all four, measured 2026-09-27.
nightqc.py.why: `sample_times` reaches `stability` ONLY through `allan.segments_by_gap`, which cuts a run where `ts[i] - ts[i-1] > k * median(deltas)` — and that median is taken over the same deltas. Both sides of the comparison scale with the axis, so the segmentation is invariant under every positive affine map of it: a scale (×1e6 here, or ×0.999) and a shift (by `t0` again, or by a diff instead of a host stamp) all leave it identical, and no absolute duration is compared anywhere on this path. The seconds the code passes are for the reader's sake; if a fixed-second threshold is ever introduced the probe test fails and these four claims have to be re-argued rather than quietly kept.

nights_index.py.probe: Ran the real `stream_stats` over a stream carrying a non-ASCII payload, and separately compared `open(encoding=None)` against `open(encoding="utf-8")` under `LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0` (locale.getencoding() → ANSI_X3.4-1968). The decoded strings differ there; the function's return does not, because it reads only the leading ASCII stamp.
nights_index.py.why:
`stream_stats` returns NUMBERS sliced from each row's LEADING ASCII stamp (`_row_seconds` reads offsets 0..22) and no decoded text reaches its output. `errors="replace"` guarantees the read cannot raise, and any non-ASCII byte sits AFTER the stamp, so a differing byte→character mapping cannot shift the slice the function actually reads. Demonstrated: a stream whose payload holds `café` returns `{fragments: 1, coverage: 1.0, gaps_s: 0.0, span_s: 2.0}` unchanged.
⚠️ I first recorded these as `environment-equivalent` on a locale argument and the gate REFUSED it as real-gap debt — correctly, because "equivalent in the environments we deploy in" is a fact about deployment, not code. I then wrote a monkeypatch test to kill them and it was VACUOUS: on Python 3.13 `open(encoding=None)` resolves via `locale.getencoding()`, not the patched `getpreferredencoding`, so both readings returned `'café'` and the test asserted nothing. Measured under `LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0`: the DECODED TEXT does differ, but the function's output does not, which is the argument above and is locale-independent.

solid_night_inputs.py.probe: 40,000 random segments at the SHIPPED magnitude (host `h` = `host.timestamp() * 1000.0` ≈ 1.79e12 floating wall-clock ms, device `d` drawn at 1e3 / 1e8 / 8.7e11 ms to cover a fresh-boot counter and a large arbitrary epoch), 3–60 anchors, drift 0 / ±60 / ±9e4 ppm, jitter σ 0.05 / 1 / 40 ms. Compared the function's OUTPUT — status and rendered reason — and, separately, the intermediates `spread`, `span_s` and `ppm`. Output identical in 40,000/40,000 for every entry here. THE MAGNITUDE IS THE POINT: float cancellation depends on the operand ratio, so the same probe sampled at ±1e6 reports exact equality where the shipped code drifts, and vice versa. Two SIBLING mutants of these same two lines did NOT survive this probe — `r0 = seg[0][0] + seg[0][1]` (1/40,000 rendered differences) and `(h - d) + r0` (21/40,000) — and are NOT excused here: they are killed by `test_the_residual_is_measured_about_THIS_segments_first_anchor_and_keeps_its_precision`.
solid_night_inputs.py.why: The first anchor of the SEGMENT defines both origins, and every consumer of `res` reads only DIFFERENCES: `spread` is max − min, `span_s` is last − first, `ppm` is a median-of-ends difference. A constant added to every element therefore cancels in all three, and re-indexing `seg[0]` to `seg[1]`, or re-origining onto the other member of the same anchor, IS such a constant. In IEEE754 it also stays exact: the re-origined operands sit within a factor of two of each other, so the subtraction is Sterbenz-exact — unlike the two sibling mutants that ADD two wall-clock-magnitude numbers and so carry the residual at ≈3.6e12 with a 4.9e-4 ms ULP. FALSIFY THIS by finding a consumer of `res` that reads an absolute value rather than a difference; there is none today.

solid_night.py.op: a different multiplier in the sample fixture's per-row device OFFSET
solid_night.py.probe: The fixture's four stated properties were measured on the bytes under this mutant and all four hold: `test_the_SAMPLE_FIXTURE_carries_the_four_properties_it_needs` passes, and so does `test_the_SAMPLE_is_a_night_that_passes_EVERY_band`. Nine of ten hand-applied mutations of this same layout DO die on those two tests (the offset's sign, a zero modulus, a per-row instead of per-frame offset, a negative jitter, a shifted frame boundary, a changed row count, a changed sample period); this one and only this one survives them.
solid_night.py.why: THE MULTIPLIER IS A FREE PARAMETER AND THE PROPERTY IS WHAT IS REQUIRED. The offset exists so the device column is not a DRAWN counter (`clock.js CK_AXIS_DRAWN_SHARE`): what the fixture owes is that no modal delta reaches `TB_DRAWN_SHARE`, that the counter stays monotone, that it starts at 0 and that it ends within one offset of the nominal span. 7919 and 7920 are both coprime-enough to 211 to spread the deltas across the same range, and `(0 * k) % 211` is 0 for either, so every one of those four holds identically. Pinning the multiplier would be pinning an arbitrary choice as if it were a requirement. FALSIFY THIS by finding a multiplier the fixture's properties hold for and the band still reads as drawn — then the properties are the thing that is incomplete, and the fix is another property, not a test of this literal.

solid_night.py.op: the `settled` flag's FALSE replaced by NONE at the compose call
solid_night.py.probe: No probe: the receiver tests the argument for FALSINESS, so the two values take the same branch for every input. Confirmed by running the full `tests/test_solid_night.py` against the mutant — 47 passed, byte-identical verdict object, including the `not settled` reason and the run's `pending` night that `monitor.html` reads.
solid_night.py.why: `compose` branches on `if not settled:` and returns the UNKNOWN `not settled` verdict there, so `False` and `None` are the SAME INPUT to the only code that reads it. The parameter is annotated `settled: bool`, which says what a caller should pass; it does not make the two distinguishable at runtime, and `pending_verdict`'s whole contract is that this call is never settled. Writing `settled=False` rather than a falsy stand-in is a statement to the READER, and that is the right reason to keep it. FALSIFY THIS by making `compose` distinguish an UNSTATED settle from a stated False — an `is False` test, or a three-valued settle where None means 'not known yet' — at which point the difference becomes real and this entry is wrong.
